# PD-1 Inhibitor Resistance — ACME Q2 2026

## Background
PD-1 inhibitor resistance has emerged as a critical challenge in melanoma and NSCLC.
Approximately 40-60% of initial responders develop acquired resistance within 2 years.
This pack reviews mechanisms, biomarkers, and combinatorial strategies under active investigation.

## Mechanism of Action
PD-1 binds to PD-L1 expressed on tumor cells, delivering an inhibitory signal that
attenuates T-cell receptor signaling. Antibody blockade (pembrolizumab, nivolumab) restores
T-cell effector function. Resistance involves loss of antigen presentation (B2M loss),
impaired interferon signaling (JAK1/JAK2 mutations), and upregulation of compensatory checkpoints.

## Biomarkers of Resistance
Tumor mutational burden, microsatellite instability, and gene expression signatures
(IFN-gamma, T-cell inflamed) correlate with response. Loss of HLA class I and beta-2-microglobulin
mutations are validated mechanisms of acquired resistance.

## Trials in Progress
KEYNOTE-789, CheckMate-9DW, and the LAG-3 combination trial RELATIVITY-047 are active.
The combination of relatlimab + nivolumab showed a 10-month PFS in melanoma.

## Safety Signals
Immune-related adverse events (irAEs) include pneumonitis (3-5%), colitis (8-12%),
and endocrinopathies. Combination regimens roughly double the grade 3+ irAE rate.

## Conclusions
The next 18 months will see readouts from at least four pivotal combination trials.
ACME should prioritize biomarker-driven enrollment and adjacent IO partnerships.
